meta.title: [Core] Freeze gc during cuda graph capture to speed up init
meta.body_summary: Freeze garbage collection during CUDA graph capture to dramatically speed up initialization, e.g., Qwen3-0.6B capture from 35s to 2s.

perf_labels.notes: Codex proposed gc.collect monkey-patching; after review feedback switched to gc.freeze and got merged with benchmark showing 35s→2s on Qwen3-0.6B.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 129,205 changed lines, this is an unusually large PR by absolute volume, but the massive churn is almost entirely from a merge commit that removes obsolete spec_decode tests and other files; the actual performance change is only ~42 lines added/modified in gpu_model_runner.py. The overall size is atypical for a perf PR and would normally be a red flag, but in context it's a side-effect of mainline rebase and cleanup. The merge outcome is consistent with a lightweight, well-benchmarked optimization that received approval despite the noisy diff.

review_details.concern_detail: Gemini bot and WoosukKwon flagged the unconventional monkey-patching; maintainers guided towards gc.freeze after exploring gc.disable and throttled gc.collect.
review_details.performance_claim: Freezing gc during CUDA graph capture speeds up initialization dramatically, e.g., Qwen3-0.6B graph capture from 35s to 2s.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: Codex initially used unittest.mock.patch to suppress gc.collect, which is non-idiomatic in production code and poorly communicated intent. The maintainers guided the design through gc.disable and eventually gc.freeze. The agent required iterative feedback to land on the optimal solution, illustrating a process boundary where AI-generated code needs human architectural guidance.

detection_detail.code_reading: Gemini bot and WoosukKwon reviewed the code for idiomatic Python and suggested using gc module directly or gc.freeze.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: PR body includes concrete before/after timing for a specific model; the benchmark is easily reproducible by running vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: After CHANGES_REQUESTED, the approach shifted from monkey-patching to gc.freeze and added an env var to disable the optimization if needed.

core_change_summary.description: In vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py, added a freeze_gc() context manager that calls gc.collect() once before CUDA graph capture, then freezes all existing objects from being scanned during subsequent automatic garbage collections inside the capture loop. The freeze/unfreeze is controlled by VLLM_ENABLE_CUDAGRAPH_GC env var (defaults to disabling freeze, i.e., requires explicit opt-in to revert to old behavior).
core_change_summary.secondary_note: The massive 198-file diff is from a merge of main branch; the core perf change is isolated to gpu_model_runner.py (~42 lines net change).
change_trajectory: Initial commit: suppress gc.collect via monkey-patching unittest.mock.patch.
Switch to gc.freeze/unfreeze approach as suggested by reviewers.
Merge main to resolve conflicts (brings large test suite refactor).
Add VLLM_ENABLE_CUDAGRAPH_GC env var for fallback.

review_signals.summary: Suggested using gc.disable/enable instead of monkey-patching gc.collect with unittest.mock.patch.
review_signals.action_taken: mgoin replied that gc.disable gave minimal benefit; approach later evolved.

review_signals.summary: Requested a more proper fix by modifying the piecewise backend's gc.collect, but later discussion led to gc.freeze approach.
review_signals.action_taken: After discussion, WoosukKwon approved the gc.freeze solution.

review_signals.summary: Suggested doing gc.collect() once then gc.freeze() before graph capture, which may eliminate need for periodic manual collections.
Approved, noting the numbers are awesome, and requested an env var to disable the new behavior as a safety measure.
Suggested moving freeze_gc context manager to utils.py.
review_signals.action_taken: mgoin agreed to refactor in a separate PR.

collaboration_trajectory: PR opened with monkey-patching approach to suppress gc.collect during CUDA graph capture.
Gemini bot review flagged non-idiomatic import of unittest.mock.patch.
Maintainer WoosukKwon CHANGES_REQUESTED, suggesting an alternative fix in the piecewise backend.
Discussion on PR comments explored throttled gc.collect and gc.disable, with benchmarks for various intervals.
Maintainer njhill suggested gc.collect + gc.freeze approach, which was adopted.
Refactored to gc.freeze, added benchmark results showing 35s→2s.
Maintainer zou3519 approved, requested optional env var for safety; env var added.
Post-merge comment suggested moving the helper to utils.py, accepted for future PR.
Merged after ~6 days of active iteration.
